title: Partner listing launch scripts and risk checklist
body:
Purpose and context:
This working doc collects launch-facing scripts, short-form copy variants, required artifacts, and a compact risk checklist for publishing Redwood Inference on cloud marketplaces (AWS/GCP/Azure) with partner-managed listings. The goal is a single-page reference the GTM/partnership ops team can use during listing submission windows and the first 30 days of live traffic.

Audience segmentation (how to position the listing copy):
- Developer-first: emphasize SDKs, latency/cost controls, sample code and fast API keys. Short tagline and quick bullets.
- Platform/IT buyer: focus on security, VPC/private deployment options, compliance, and enterprise SLAs.
- Product/exec buyer: highlight business outcomes (reduce inference cost, predictable latency, rollout controls).

One-liners (choose one per marketplace):
- Dev-focused: "High-performance LLM inference with predictable latency — deploy hosted, dedicated, or private."
- Enterprise-focused: "Secure, SLA-backed inference with dedicated capacity and private deployment options for regulated teams."
- Outcome-focused: "Lower inference unit cost and guarantee latency SLOs for production LLM apps."

Short description variants (80–130 characters):
1) "Flexible LLM inference: hosted API, reserved GPU capacity, and private deployments — production-grade."
2) "Ship LLM features with predictable latency and cost — SDKs, rollout controls, and observability."
3) "Enterprise inference platform: private VPC, KMS/HSM support, and SLA-backed dedicated capacity."

Bullet list (features — keep to 6 max for marketplace UI):
- Hosted REST/SDK API for generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking
- Dedicated GPU pools with autoscaling and burst capacity
- Private deployment (VPC & on-prem) with audit logs and KMS integrations
- Smart routing & model variant fallbacks for high availability
- Cost controls: batching, KV caching, and quantization recommendations
- Console: model rollouts, token-level cost/latency breakdowns, and tracing

Three 1-paragraph marketing blurbs (developer / IT / exec):
- Developer blurb: "Redwood Inference gives engineers a simple REST and SDK interface to production LLMs. Start with a hosted API key, then scale to dedicated capacity when you need throughput guarantees. Built-in client libraries, streaming responses, and sample apps make prototyping fast — and runtime optimizations keep token costs under control."
- IT/Platform blurb: "Operate inference safely and predictably. Redwood Private runs in your VPC or on-prem, integrates with KMS/HSM, and emits audit logs for compliance. For teams needing predictable throughput, Dedicated capacity provides reserved GPU pools with SLA-backed latency targets and autoscaling policies."
- Executive blurb: "Ship LLM features faster while controlling cost and risk. Redwood helps teams trade off model quality, latency, and unit economics with observability and automated recommendations that reduce inference spend without sacrificing performance."

Snippet library (short CTAs and in-list copy):
- CTA primary: "Start a free trial — 14 days of credits"
- CTA secondary: "Request a demo & capacity estimate"
- Pricing microcopy: "Usage-based hosted API; reserved capacity contracts for Dedicated; enterprise licensing for Private."
- Security microcopy: "SOC2-ready controls, KMS/HSM integrations, VPC peering and audit logs."

Marketplace-specific preflight checklist (must be confirmed before submission):
- Legal & billing:
  - Confirm SKU mapping and seller pricing (list price, free tier credit amounts).
  - Billing tests with partner sandbox account for metering and chargeback.
  - Confirm tax & compliance statements required by vendor.
- Technical & infra:
  - Validate API endpoint domains and allowed CORS origins for marketplace proxies.
  - Provide SaaS healthcheck endpoint (status page / readiness probe) for listing.
  - Confirm region availability mapping between our infra and marketplace regions.
- Security & compliance:
  - Upload SOC2 summary and contact for security reviews.
  - Provide KMS integration notes and private deployment architecture diagrams.
- Content & assets:
  - Screenshots: Console model dashboard, rollout page, and cost breakdown.
  - Short demo video (30–60s) and one-page PDF datasheet.
  - Three tagline/copy variants in approved language.
- Operations & support:
  - SLA summary and escalation path (on-call contact, enterprise support tiers).
  - Enable marketplace support routing + internal runbook link.

Launch scripts (short templates to use in comms):
- Internal ops alert (prelaunch, 48h):
  Subject: Marketplace listing go-live window — [Vendor] — [Date]
  Body: Quick heads-up: we plan to publish the [Vendor] marketplace listing on [Date]. Confirmed: SKU, pricing, screenshots, demo video, and billing sandbox tests are green. Ops/infra: please stand by 30–90m after publish for checkout validation and ingestion logs. Slack #marketplace will be primary channel.

- Customer-facing in-product banner copy (short):
  "Try faster, cheaper LLM inference — now available through [Vendor Marketplace]. Click to claim trial credits or request a dedicated capacity estimate."

- Partner support reply template (for post-publish issues):
  Thanks — we see the error on the marketplace integration. Our ingestion team has opened INC-[id]. Immediate mitigation: switch routing to Hosted fallback variant for impacted SKUs; we will coordinate rollback if required. ETA for fix: 2 hours.

Compact risk checklist and mitigations (first 30 days):
- Risk: Mispriced SKU causing unexpected invoice spikes.
  Mitigation: Keep an internal billing throttle for first 7 days, daily metering review, auto-alert on >20% variance vs forecast.
- Risk: Marketplace proxies strip important headers and break auth.
  Mitigation: Preflight test accounts and a minimal sample integration to validate headers; provide vendor-specific auth guide.
- Risk: Listing content mismatch (screenshots vs deployed features).
  Mitigation: Final content freeze 72h before publish and a single owner (marketing) to approve assets.
- Risk: Support routing confusion between Redwood and marketplace support.
  Mitigation: Publish clear support triage matrix in listing and enable internal–vendor escalation call cadence (D+0, D+1).

Acceptance gates (go/no-go criteria for publish):
- All legal/billing paperwork signed and test charges processed in partner sandbox.
- Required screenshots, video, and datasheet uploaded and validated in vendor preview.
- Billing SKU mapping confirmed and test invoice validated.
- Support playbook published and on-call person identified for 72h post-launch.

Operational runbook references (links to internal resources):
- Marketplace playbook (long): https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/MP-1234
- Billing runbook: JIRA-9876
- Support triage matrix: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/MP-1950

Notes / open questions (work-in-progress):
- Do we want a separate free-tier SKU for developer trials vs trial credits applied at account creation? Pros/cons discussed below.
- Which marketplaces require a reseller contract vs simple marketplace listing? Need legal confirmation before final SKU mapping.
- Translate main tagline into DE/FR/JP — prioritize DE & FR for Q1.

Quick decisions needed from stakeholders (owners listed):
- Marketing: pick primary one-liner for all vendors (owner: Elena Ross)
- Finance: confirm SKU price floor and trial credit amount (owner: Marcus Lee)
- Legal: confirm reseller vs listing contract requirements per vendor (owner: Priya Nambiar)

This doc is intentionally concise — use it as the single-pane checklist for launch calls. Append or push final assets to the Confluence playbook (MP-1234) once green-lit for publish.
